facts.label: The facts of one incident, filled in by code (klaxon.agent.postmortem) from a gated run's saved evidence: its run.json, the gate's request, decision and log, and the loop's trace. Each fact says where it comes from. The incident: a fault injected on purpose into a payments system on one machine, with synthetic data and a simulated provider, so no real money.

run.title: Payments counted twice in the books
run.what_it_was: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, duplicate-delivery, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, offered one write action (rollback_deploy), which runs only if a person approves it at the gate, and stopped on diagnosed after 4 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Klaxon asked at the approval gate to act on its diagnosis; the request was approved with make approve (the request's id typed at a terminal), and the action ran: redeploy ledger-consumer: LEDGER_HANDLER naive -> idempotent, LEDGER_BAD_EVENTS dead_letter (unchanged). Code, not the model, then verified it (klaxon.agent.verify): passed; the cause is removed, and the money is not right. The fault's cause was removed by Klaxon: its rollback (Klaxon, approved request r-33b5) removed the cause, and the harness's clearing then found the good settings running, and changed nothing.

timeline.what: The alert rules were quiet at 2 evaluations in a row, and the money check passed: the stack was ready for the fault.

The fault's injection began, on purpose (klaxon.faults): a deploy of ledger-consumer with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive. It took 2.3 s. The deploy log has it as deploy 127, by klaxon.faults, at 2026-11-17T04:24:19Z.

The alert MoneyCheckFailed fired, raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed: The money check failed 2 of its 5 invariants: posted_exactly_once (7 findings), matches_provider (8 findings). By its count, our ledger is $461.00 ahead of the provider's balance.

Klaxon's loop began to investigate the alert: claude-opus-5-5 through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, with read-only tools, offered one write action (rollback_deploy) that runs only if a person approves it.
The loop stopped: diagnosed (confidence 0.85), after 4 steps and 3 tool calls, in 25.4 s.
The money check right before the request: 9 events counted more than once, 9 payments whose books differ from the provider's; our books $559.21 ahead of the provider's balance.

Klaxon asked to act, at the approval gate: request r-33b5, redeploy ledger-consumer: LEDGER_HANDLER naive -> idempotent, LEDGER_BAD_EVENTS dead_letter (unchanged). It was open until 2026-11-17T04:35:01Z. Its undo: going back to LEDGER_HANDLER=naive would deploy a known-bad setting: Klaxon will not; a person can, by hand.
Request r-33b5 was approved with make approve: typed at a terminal.
The action ran: deploy 128 of ledger-consumer in the deploy log, by Klaxon, approved request r-33b5, with LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent, LEDGER_BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter.
The money check right after the action: 20 events counted more than once, 20 payments whose books differ from the provider's; our books $1,178.22 ahead of the provider's balance.
Health, by code: 2 rounds of the rules and the containers, from 2026-11-17T04:26:15Z to 2026-11-17T04:26:31Z: healthy.
The later money check, at least a minute after the action: 20 events counted more than once, 20 payments whose books differ from the provider's; our books $1,178.22 ahead of the provider's balance.
Verification, by code and not by the model: passed.

The harness's clearing, its safety net, asked for the good settings of ledger-consumer (LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent, LEDGER_BAD_EVENTS=dead_letter). The fault's cause was removed by Klaxon: its rollback (Klaxon, approved request r-33b5) removed the cause, and the harness's clearing then found the good settings running, and changed nothing.
The rules read the stack again after the clearing: the alert MoneyCheckFailed fired; the money check failed: posted_exactly_once 20, matches_provider 21; our books $1,178.22 ahead of the provider's.

model_words.note: the loop's own words, from a model: data, not checked by code
model_words.hypothesis: ledger-consumer was redeployed at 04:24:17Z, 17 seconds before the alert, with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive. This handler books every Kafka message it receives and never checks whether that event_id was already posted. The provider resends webhooks until they are acknowledged, so the same event can reach provider-events more than once. Each copy then becomes a new ledger transaction. evt_000308 was booked three times from three offsets (100, 101 and 103). Six other events, five charges and one refund, were booked twice. The result is $461.00 of extra provider_clearing balance. The ledger still balances because each duplicate is a full double entry. Our payments and refunds still match the provider, which places the fault in ledger posting only. The duplicate refund also explains why pay_000217 nets to 1 cent in our ledger against $24.56 at the provider.
model_words.fix_summary: Roll ledger-consumer back to its previous settings, which should restore the idempotent handler that dedups on event_id. Then repair the ledger as a separate step. Reverse the extra transactions for the 7 events in c1 (for example 255, 266, 272, 273, 297 and the extras for evt_000298 and evt_000308), keeping one posting per event. Re-run the money check to confirm that posted_exactly_once and matches_provider pass.
model_words.blast_radius: The ledger-consumer container is recreated, so ledger posting pauses briefly. Kafka holds the events and the consumer group resumes from its committed offset, so nothing should be lost. payment-confirmer and payments-api are unaffected. The rollback only stops new duplicates. The $461.00 already over-booked stays wrong until the data repair is done. Left open: I did not confirm the exact previous LEDGER_HANDLER value, or whether any duplicates predate the 04:24:17 deploy. The transaction ids suggest they are all recent.
model_words.rollback_plan: If the rolled-back consumer misbehaves, for example by failing to post or by building up lag, redeploy ledger-consumer with its current settings. Do this only while the ledger is watched, because the current naive handler will keep double-posting. Hold off the ledger repair until the consumer is stable, and do it as reversing entries so it can itself be undone.

narrative.summary: On 2026-11-17, a fault was injected on purpose into a payments system on one machine, with synthetic data and no real money. The fault was a deploy of the ledger consumer with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive, which booked webhooks that the provider resent a second time. The alert MoneyCheckFailed fired 17.3 s after the fault. Klaxon diagnosed the cause, and a rule graded that diagnosis as naming the cause. Klaxon then asked at the approval gate to roll the ledger consumer back. Request r-33b5 was approved, and deploy 128 restored LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent. Verification by code passed: the system was healthy and the cause was removed. The money was still not right. The last money check found 20 events counted more than once, and our books $1,178.22 ahead of the provider's balance. That damage stays until a person repairs it.
narrative.timeline: At 04:24:16 UTC the alert rules were quiet and the money check passed. The fault was then injected as deploy 127 of the ledger consumer at 04:24:19, with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive. The alert MoneyCheckFailed fired at 04:24:34, 17.3 s after the fault. Klaxon's loop began at 04:24:35 and stopped at 04:25:00, diagnosed with confidence 0.85, after 4 steps and 3 tool calls in 25.4 s. Klaxon made request r-33b5 at 04:25:01, open until 04:35:01. It was approved at 04:26:11, after 70 s. The rollback ran as deploy 128 at 04:26:14, 100 s after the alert and 115 s after the fault's deploy. Health checks ran from 04:26:15 to 04:26:31 and found the system healthy. A later money check ran at 04:27:14. Verification passed 178 s after the fault. The harness's clearing came 178.2 s after the fault, found the good settings already running, and changed nothing. At 04:28:45 the rules read the stack again, and MoneyCheckFailed fired again.
narrative.impact: No real money and no real customers were involved. At the alert, at 04:24:34, the money check failed 2 of its 5 invariants: posted_exactly_once had 7 findings and matches_provider had 8. Our ledger was $461.00 ahead of the provider's balance. Right before the request, at 04:25:00, 9 events were counted more than once, and our books were $559.21 ahead. Right after the action, at 04:26:14, 20 events were counted more than once, 20 payments' books differed from the provider's, and our books were $1,178.22 ahead. The later check at 04:27:14 found the same. After the clearing, at 04:28:45, the rules found posted_exactly_once 20 and matches_provider 21, still $1,178.22 ahead. The evidence does not explain why matches_provider showed 21 there but 20 payments in the later check. The synthetic clients saw no failures. 1021 payments arrived and 1021 succeeded, with 0 refused and 0 left unknown. Refunds: 103 succeeded and 0 were refused. The clients retried 35 times.
narrative.cause: The recorded cause was a deploy of the ledger consumer without its dedupe, with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive. Every webhook that the provider sent again, after an acknowledgement it never got, was booked a second time. Those extra postings put our books ahead of the provider's balance, and the money check raised MoneyCheckFailed. Klaxon's diagnosis said the ledger consumer had been redeployed with the naive handler, which did not check whether an event was already posted, and that the provider resends unacknowledged webhooks. A rule, not a person or a model, graded the diagnosis as naming the cause. It named the place, the lost dedupe, the resent webhooks and the deploy, and its fix fit the remedy. The rule reads words, not meaning. The diagnosis gave a time for the deploy that differs from the deploy log's time. It also said it had not confirmed the previous handler setting, or whether any duplicates predated the deploy.
narrative.response: Klaxon investigated with tools that only read, and was offered one write action, rollback_deploy. It asked at the gate with request r-33b5: redeploy the ledger consumer with LEDGER_HANDLER changed from naive to idempotent, and LEDGER_BAD_EVENTS left as dead_letter. The request was approved at 04:26:11 with make approve, typed at a terminal. The gate's log records how the decision was made, not who made it. The plan says only Aravind approves Klaxon's actions. Deploy 128 ran at 04:26:14. Code, not the model, then verified the result in 61.1 s. It found every container healthy, and found that nothing the provider made after the action was booked wrong. It also found the money not right. The evidence leaves open why the health check reported the books rule quiet while the money checks around it failed, and why MoneyCheckFailed fired again at 04:28:45.
narrative.repairs: The damage already booked is still owed. The last money check, at 04:27:14, found 20 events counted more than once, 20 payments whose books differ from the provider's, and our books $1,178.22 ahead of the provider's balance. Its first examples include event evt_000308, posted 3 times, and events such as evt_000251 and evt_000298, posted 2 times. The rollback stopped new duplicates but repaired nothing. The recorded remedy is to reverse each double posting. That is a write, so it needs approval. Repairs that move money are not among Klaxon's actions, so a person must make them. A person should also confirm why the alert fired again after the clearing, and settle the different counts for matches_provider.
